key_insight: X-FEMR makes black-box EHR foundation models more interpretable by using a Transformer surrogate to reveal which patient-history tokens most influence predictions.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a practical explainability layer for clinical AI systems, helping improve trust, auditability, and model debugging in downstream healthcare deployment.
method: Train a Transformer-based surrogate on FEMR input-output pairs for two prediction tasks.
Preserve temporal dynamics while approximating FEMR behavior.
Extract the most influential tokens and score their clinical alignment with validated features.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the surrogate closely matches FEMR predictions and that token-level explanations show good alignment with clinical knowledge across the evaluated tasks.
watch_item: Because explanations come from a surrogate model, fidelity to the original FEMR may vary outside the evaluated tasks or patient populations.
paper_title: X-FEMR: A Token-level Explainable Approach for Electronic Health Records Foundation Models using Transformer-based Models
